scope: One shared exterior for Luz Station and the Museum of the Portuguese Language, with the restored station wings, clock tower, street canopy and attached platform shed.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum archive identifies the 1901 Victorian station and the 2021 reopening retaining its original character.

Beatriz Mugayar Kühl describes the two physical sections, rolled steel and cast-iron train shed, 39 by 150 metre roof, sunken tracks, the western clock tower about 60 metres above track level and 3.30-metre dials.
The museum documents current exterior conservation of the same standing station.
